items.title: No omega-stable type of limit Morley rank has nonminimality degree equal to the Morley-sequence invariant together with definable Morley sequences
items.author: John T. Baldwin; James Freitag; Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the theorem labelled nmdegmbdefinablemorleyproperty at source lines 2887-2890: an omega-stable theory has no type p with RM(p) a limit ordinal, nmdeg(p) = F_Mb(p), and p having definable Morley sequences. The argument turns on a strict Morley-rank gap: a single formula phi has to be extracted by compactness out of the set sigma of formulas that fork over A at every realization of q = (p) to the n-th tensor power, and lambda-prime = RM(phi(x, b_0 ... b_n) union p(x)) has to be shown strictly below lambda = RM(p), after which the limit ordinal lambda supplies lambda-prime-prime with lambda-prime < lambda-prime-prime < lambda and a type q in S(B) of that rank (source line 2893). The contradiction then makes one sequence play two roles at once: a Morley sequence in q over B is not a Morley sequence over A, since Kim's lemma would otherwise make B independent from a_0 over A, yet precisely its failure to be Morley over A makes phi(a_n, a_0 ... a_{n-1}) true and forces RM(phi(x, a_0 ... a_n) union p(x)) to be at least lambda-prime-prime, against the A-equivalence of a_0 ... a_{n-1} and b_0 ... b_{n-1}. The reduction to an algebraically closed base in T^eq, the stationarity of p and the two-sided reading of the single formula phi are compressed into one paragraph and are not a routine unfolding of definitions.
